raw_text:
Review README.md and /src files for repository purpose/structure and update this overview.

.NET 10.0 (`net10.0`); latest C#; nullable/implicit usings; `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`; warning 1591 suppressed via `NoWarn`. Structure: `src/`, `tests/`, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `Template.slnx`. Uses `ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true`; versions in [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props); project references omit versions; add packages with `<PackageVersion Include="PackageName" Version="x.y.z" />`.

Use file-scoped namespaces, 2 spaces, CRLF, UTF-8 BOM, Allman braces; `_myField`, PascalCase constants, apparent `var`, `I` interfaces, `Async` methods. Always use `{}` except single-line exits (`return`, `throw`); `csharp_prefer_braces = true`; primary constructors preferred and ALWAYS assign to readonly fields; prefer top-level statements, pattern matching, expression-bodied properties/indexers/accessors (NOT methods). Run `dotnet format`; use analyzers from [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props); consider NSDepCop.

Use appsettings, `IConfiguration`, `IOptions<T>`, typed settings, User Secrets. Never hardcode sensitive information in source code. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging`, suitable levels, context, structured logs; avoid sensitive data; correlation IDs when possible.

Follow OWASP guidelines for secure coding practices. Validate and sanitize all user inputs. Use parameterized queries or ORM features to prevent SQL injection. Implement proper authentication and authorization mechanisms. Use HTTPS for all communications. Use `Ardalis.GuardClauses` non-UI; prefer `FluentValidation` for complex/UI validation. UI invalid inputs must produce user-friendly errors; non-UI invalid inputs must throw appropriate guard-clause exceptions. HTTP methods should return suitable status codes for non-success results.

Use DI, composition, async I/O, focused classes/methods (<20 lines), parameter objects over >4 arguments; prefer REPR/FastEndpoints and DDD; `*Request`/`*Response`, `*Command`/`*Query`, DTOs not entities, `*Details`/`*Summary`; avoid colocating interfaces/implementations. Write unit testable code. Offer to add tests to generated code if applicable - place such tests in the `tests/` folder. Only test code that you control and that has business logic; do not test framework code.

Production projects go in `src/`, test projects in `tests/`; tests use `xUnit`. Run `dotnet run --project src/YourProject/YourProject.csproj`. Arrange-Act-Assert (whitespace only); mirrored feature folders; no “Tests” class suffix; `[Fact]`, `[Theory]`/`[InlineData]`; `ClassName_MethodName.cs`; sentence-like names; separate unit/integration projects. Prefer NSubstitute and Shouldly. Avoid commercially licensed testing libraries (e.g. FluentAssertions, Moq).

Use Markdown, headings, syntax-highlighted snippets, linting, and blank lines around lists/code listings. Reference [.editorconfig](.editorconfig), [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props), [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props), [.gitignore](.gitignore).
